👇 We built a portfolio robo-advisor that tracks the market, winning 1st place at Waterloo's annual CFM Case Competition! While beating the market often gets the spotlight, doing so consistently is difficult, even for professionals. In practice, many investors are better served by portfolios that prioritize stability, safety, and controlled exposure rather than chasing high returns. So, along with Jaimin Patel and Frank Lin , we built a market-tracking portfolio robo-advisor. As students, our goal wasn't to outsmart the market, but to understand how to meet it. We focused on minimizing unnecessary deviation, managing risk, and building a system that behaves predictably under real market conditions. 🛠️ What we built: - A Python-based investment engine selecting 10–25 stocks - Dynamic weight adjustments using rolling beta, volatility, covariance, and correlation - A scorecard framework benchmarking each stock directly against a blended TSX / S&P 500 index - Defensive sector tilting (e.g., Healthcare, Utilities) to stabilize performance during market noise 📈 The result? After running live for 5 trading days with continuously updated market data, our portfolio achieved a 3.23% return, finishing only 0.70% off the blended TSX/S&P 500 benchmark despite a short window and earning 1st place. What mattered most to me wasn’t just the win, but the process: - Designing signals that update daily, not in hindsight - Thinking in terms of risk, stability, and relative movement not just returns - Seeing how small modelling decisions compound when exposed to real markets I am grateful for my teammates and for a program that gives us room to experiment, compete, and learn by doing. Looking forward to building on this foundation going forward! 🔗 Links: Github repo: https://lnkd.in/eyga9erH Article: https://lnkd.in/e2MCcDrm ...more ...more

Introducing the Mercor AI Consumer Index (ACE), our benchmark for measuring how frontier models handle the everyday tasks people use AI for across Shopping, Food, Gaming, and DIY. The results show a clear gap between expectations and performance: even the top model scores only 56.1% overall, and models fail grounding checks between 29% and 62% of the time, often hallucinating basic details like prices or links. ACE introduces a methodology built for real-world reliability, with hurdle criteria that require solving the user’s core objective and grounding criteria that penalize hallucinations. We also have criteria labels that reveal where models break down: strong performance on simple quantity checks, but much weaker on nuanced judgments like Gaming compatibility and DIY safety guidance. We’re open-sourcing 80 cases on Hugging Face and our full evaluation harness on GitHub to support transparency and reproducibility. Together with APEX, our benchmarks now measure both economic value and consumer value, because AI’s usefulness depends on how well it performs even beyond the workplace. Visit: https://lnkd.in/gzZXryxM ...more ...more

We’ve doubled the size of APEX, our benchmark for assessing whether frontier models can perform economically valuable work. The benchmark evaluates four high-value jobs: investment banking associate, management consultant, big law associate, and primary care physician (MD). The eval set now includes 400 real-world cases, mirroring the deliverables professionals produce every day. What we’re seeing: - OpenAI 's GPT 5 remains the best performing model. - Investment Banking remains the hardest job we test for; even top models stay at ~60% - Models are improving. Anthropic 's Claude Opus 4.5 improved nearly 12 points over Opus 4.1. Google 's Gemini 3 Pro is fast approaching GPT 5. This demonstrates that the gap between capability and economic usefulness is still large. APEX helps quantify that gap and give labs a clear target to hill-climb. We’re also open-sourcing 100 cases (25 in each domain), as well as our eval harness. We are excited to see what you build. Read the full paper: https://lnkd.in/gfjjVDZi ...more ...more

Today, we’re opening applications for the first cohort of OpenAI Campus Leads - a global program. Apply here: https://lnkd.in/giyFQCaF I’m especially excited that we’re looking for community builders, not only technical experts. Access to AI is only a starting point. If this technology is going to expand opportunity, students everywhere need the agency and skills to use it thoughtfully - to ask good questions, exercise judgment, solve meaningful problems, and create things that matter. Campus Leads will create those spaces for peers. They’ll gather students across fields to learn and move from using ChatGPT to building with ChatGPT and Codex, through workshops, weekly building hours, and project showcases. Our team will work closely to set each Campus Lead up for success, offering them robust training in our tools, funding, swag, and access to a community of remarkable peers around the world. If this sounds like you—or a student you know—I hope you’ll apply or help us spread the word.

Say hello to Aleksandar Filipovic , a second-year Electrical Engineering student at The University of British Columbia —born and raised in Vancouver—and Software Engineering Intern at RV Tech focused on High Voltage Charging. Alek’s curiosity about how technology works started young, long before he joined UBC Baja SAE to integrate sensors onto off-road vehicles. That blend of vehicles and data made RV Tech a natural next step. In just two months, Alek built something our engineers use every day: a charging session simulation tool. EV charging bugs are often specific to individual chargers, and diagnosing them used to mean traveling to the physical charger site. Alek’s tool replays real field logs entirely on a laptop, reproducing the session with timing accurate to fractions of a second, with no travel required. He even went beyond the original brief, extending the tool to cover encrypted charge sessions too. His manager says it best: Alek pauses to think, asks the right questions, works methodically, and never loses momentum. We’re glad you’re here, Alek! ⚡
